findings.title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting breaks skipping splitting for $__range/$__range_s/$__range_ms queries
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, ...)` on line 299 before calling `querySupportsSplitting(query)` on line 300. `querySupportsSplitting` relies on `!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to detect literal `$__range`, `$__range_s`, or `$__range_ms` in `query.expr` so those queries are not split across time ranges. However, `LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables` replaces `$__range`, `$__range_s`, and `$__range_ms` (via `this.templateSrv.replace`) with concrete duration values from `scopedVars` (or leaves them already substituted), so by the time `querySupportsSplitting` runs, `query.expr` no longer contains `$__range*`. As a result, queries using `$__range`, `$__range_s`, or `$__range_ms` will now be treated as normal splittable queries and split into 1-day chunks while keeping the full-range duration in their range vector, producing completely wrong query results.
